summary: Drove a hub-spawned desktop substrate over MCP: staged RobotoMono.ttf into the writable `save` namespace, loaded it via aether.text.load_font (font_id=0), then rendered a 6-row text panel with a SINGLE aether.text.draw_batch to the aether.text mailbox — six items at distinct screen origins down a column (y=40..290), distinct colors, with rows 4 and 5 sharing one clip rect. capture_frame confirmed all six rows (coverage 0.021, bbox y=48..319). No per-string aether.text.draw was ever sent. The draw_batch schema (items vec of {font_id, text, size_pixels, color, origin:[f32;2], space, clip:Option<{x,y,w,h}>}) had to be discovered via describe_kinds because it is entirely undocumented. The first cold-pipeline one-shot capture rendered blank; it only worked after a priming send. Engine left alive with a warm atlas.

artifact.rationale: The captured frame is a completely empty flat slate-blue background. Zero text is rendered — none of the ~6 expected legible, stacked text strings appear at all. Rather than 6 rows present with correct order and no overlap, the frame shows nothing renderable in the text overlay: every row is effectively dropped/absent.

papercut.where: capture_frame with draw_batch in mails on a freshly-loaded font (cold render pipeline)
papercut.what: A naive one-shot 'load_font then capture_frame with the draw_batch in mails' rendered a completely BLANK frame (coverage 0.0, bounding box null) — nothing appeared. The identical batch rendered every row only after a prior priming draw_batch had been dispatched. It is not purely per-glyph atlas warming: the second capture rendered brand-new glyphs (B, C, D, E, v, c...) that were absent from the priming send, so a first-ever-draw pipeline/texture-realization warm-up is being missed at readback. The recipe implies a glyph shows the first frame it is requested ('the first frame a new glyph appears costs one atlas upload and every frame after is a cache hit'), so a consumer reasonably expects the single-shot capture to work — and silently gets an empty PNG.
papercut.suggested: Make the text cap's first-frame glyph upload + draw_textured_quads deterministically visible at same-tick readback (realize the lazily-created texture / activate the overlay pass before readback), or at minimum document that a cold capture must send the batch once to warm the pipeline before capture_frame.

papercut.where: aether.text.load_font on a hub-spawned substrate, following the recipe's 'put a TTF in assets, path fonts/RobotoMono.ttf' steps
papercut.what: The recipe tells you to load the font from the assets namespace ('namespace':'assets','path':'fonts/RobotoMono.ttf'), but a hub-forked substrate's assets namespace is empty (aether.fs.list returns []) — the hub does not point AETHER_ASSETS_DIR at the bundle's assets/fonts. load_font returned Err 'file read failed: NotFound'. I had to stage the TTF into the writable `save` namespace via aether.fs.write {$file:...} and load from `save` instead. The documented happy path fails out of the box in the drive/MCP medium.
papercut.suggested: Either wire hub-spawned substrates' assets namespace to a default asset dir (or the bundle fonts), or update the drive recipe to show staging a font into `save`/`config` via aether.fs.write {$file:...} and loading from there, since a fresh hub engine has no assets.

doc-gap.where: docs/guide/recipes/drawing-text.md (and SUMMARY.md text section) — learning aether.text.draw_batch
doc-gap.what: The batched surface (aether.text.draw_batch / DrawTextBatch, its items vector, and per-item origin/clip) is completely undocumented. The only text recipe covers just the single aether.text.draw kind. A fresh consumer cannot discover draw_batch, its item shape, or the shared-clip semantics from docs — I had to fall back to describe_kinds full-schema output to learn the field layout.
doc-gap.suggested: Add a 'batch a panel in one mail' section to drawing-text.md documenting draw_batch: the items vector, per-item origin/color/space/clip, that clips can be shared across items, and that the cap coalesces them into one draw_textured_quads emission.

doc-gap.where: docs/guide/recipes/drawing-text.md — 'What it does not do yet' section
doc-gap.what: The doc states 'Screen text anchors at the top-left. There is no per-draw screen origin in the vocabulary yet; the string starts at pixel (0,0).' This is stale and directly contradicts the shipped surface: BOTH aether.text.draw and aether.text.draw_batch now carry a per-item origin:[f32;2] and a clip:Option field. The example draw payloads in the same doc also omit origin/clip entirely.
doc-gap.suggested: Delete the stale 'no per-draw screen origin' bullet and update the draw example payloads to show origin and clip; note that origin now positions each string.
